section: Germany: partners' profit shares and the year of moving to or from Germany, tax year 2026
wording: This skill covers two gaps the other Germany skills leave open. wording: **Step 3: trade tax and the § 35 credit.** A commercial partnership pays trade tax itself (§ 5 GewStG; see de-trade-tax). Its trade income starts from the profit fixed in Step 1, Sondervergütungen and special items included (§ 7 GewStG). A partner's share of profit from another partnership is taken out again (§ 9 no. 2 GewStG), because that partnership pays its own trade tax. The base amount, the trade tax actually payable and each partner's share of both are fixed in the same determination (§ 35(2) sentence 1 and (4) EStG). Each partner's share follows the general profit-sharing key, ignoring advance shares (§ 35(2) sentence 2). The BMF letter on § 35 says the same for Sondervergütungen and for results of special and supplementary balance sheets (BMF 3 November 2016, Rn. 22), and a partner that cannot use the credit, such as a GmbH general partner, still takes its key share (Rn. 24). A managing partner's Sondervergütung therefore gives no extra credit. The partner's credit is the lowest of: 4 × share of the base amount; the tax on trade income in the partner's own return (positive trade income / all positive income × tariff tax, § 35(1) sentence 2); the share of trade tax actually payable. Unused credit is lost.

wording: **Step 4: losses of limited partners (§ 15a EStG).** A limited partner's loss share cannot be set against other income, or carried back or forward under § 10d, so far as it creates or increases a negative capital account. Exception: losses up to the amount by which the registered liability exceeds the contribution actually paid, if the partner is entered in the commercial register, the liability is proven, and a claim under it is not excluded by contract or unlikely (§ 15a(1) sentences 2 and 3). The blocked loss is only set against later profits from the same partnership (§ 15a(2)). It is fixed each year in a separate notice (§ 15a(4)). Withdrawals that create or increase a negative capital account are added as profit, up to the losses that were deductible in that year and the ten years before (§ 15a(3)). The same rule applies to atypical silent partners and to GbR partners whose liability is excluded or unlikely (§ 15a(5)).

wording: **Step 5: the retained-profits option (§ 34a EStG), in summary.** A partner whose profit is computed from balance sheets (§ 4(1) or § 5) and whose share is over 10% or over EUR 10,000 may apply, per partnership share and per year, for profit left in the business to be taxed at 28.25% in 2026 instead of the tariff. Profit left in = profit less the positive balance of withdrawals over contributions, plus trade tax (§ 34a(2)). When later withdrawals exceed later profits, the amount fixed as liable to recapture is taxed at 25% (§ 34a(4)). The surcharge applies to both. The calculation is not set out here: refer.

wording: **Step 3: trade tax and the § 35 credit.** A commercial partnership pays trade tax itself (§ 5 GewStG; see de-trade-tax). Its trade income starts from the profit fixed in Step 1, Sondervergütungen and special items included (§ 7 GewStG). A partner's share of profit from another partnership is taken out again (§ 9 no. 2 GewStG), because that partnership pays its own trade tax. The base amount, the trade tax actually payable and each partner's share of both are fixed in the same determination (§ 35(2) sentence 1 and (4) EStG). Each partner's share follows the general profit-sharing key, ignoring advance shares (§ 35(2) sentence 2). The BMF letter on § 35 says the same for Sondervergütungen and for results of special and supplementary balance sheets (BMF 3 November 2016, Rn. 22), and a partner that cannot use the credit, such as a GmbH general partner, still takes its key share (Rn. 24). A managing partner's Sondervergütung therefore gives no extra credit. The partner's credit is the lowest of: 4 × share of the base amount; the tax on trade income in the partner's own return (positive trade income / all positive income × tariff tax, § 35(1) sentence 2); the share of trade tax actually payable. Unused credit is lost.

wording: **Step 4: losses of limited partners (§ 15a EStG).** A limited partner's loss share cannot be set against other income, or carried back or forward under § 10d, so far as it creates or increases a negative capital account. Exception: losses up to the amount by which the registered liability exceeds the contribution actually paid, if the partner is entered in the commercial register, the liability is proven, and a claim under it is not excluded by contract or unlikely (§ 15a(1) sentences 2 and 3). The blocked loss is only set against later profits from the same partnership (§ 15a(2)). It is fixed each year in a separate notice (§ 15a(4)). Withdrawals that create or increase a negative capital account are added as profit, up to the losses that were deductible in that year and the ten years before (§ 15a(3)). The same rule applies to atypical silent partners and to GbR partners whose liability is excluded or unlikely (§ 15a(5)).
